description: Fig. 4 is a five-panel statistical figure quantifying the grain structure of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels after solution treatment. Panels (a)-(d) are purple relative-proportion histograms with y-axis "Relative proportion (%)" and x-axis "Grain size (µm)": (a) S0 over 0-100 µm, with a broken y-axis (ticks 0, 2, 4, axis-break symbol, then 55, 60, 65) so that one dominant bar just above 0 µm (near 59%) remains visible; printed annotation "Average grain size=7.6 µm". (b) S950, y 0-50%, annotation "Average grain size=8.7 µm". (c) S1050, y 0-25%, "Average grain size=21.1 µm". (d) S1150, x extended to 150 µm, y 0-25%, "Average grain size=32.0 µm", with a visibly broadened distribution. Panel (e) is a dual-axis plot: left axis "Grain boundary density (µm/µm²)" (0.00-0.20), right axis "Average KAM value" (0.0-2.0), x categories S0, S950, S1050, S1150; purple bars are ATBs and green bars HAGBs (legend top right), with printed values 0.044/0.035 (S0), 0.146/0.114 (S950), 0.061/0.029 (S1050), 0.040/0.019 (S1150), plus a red line with circular markers whose height drops steeply from S0 to a low plateau across the solution-treated samples. The figure demonstrates that solution treatment homogenises and coarsens the grains while sharply reducing residual stress (KAM) and grain-boundary density.

subfigures.description: Grain-size histogram for sample S0: y-axis 'Relative proportion (%)' broken between 4 and 55, x-axis 'Grain size (µm)' 0-100. A single tall bar at ~1-2 µm reaching ~59% dominates; remaining bars stay below ~5%. Printed annotation 'Average grain size=7.6 µm'.
Grain-size histogram for S950, y 0-50%, x 0-100 µm, bars decreasing monotonically from ~43% at ~2 µm out to ~20 µm. Printed annotation 'Average grain size=8.7 µm'.
Grain-size histogram for S1050, y 0-25%, x 0-100 µm, peak near 21% at a few µm with a tail up to ~100 µm. Printed annotation 'Average grain size=21.1 µm'.
Grain-size histogram for S1150, y 0-25%, x extended to 150 µm, broadest distribution with peak ~20% near 5 µm and low bars spread to ~140 µm. Printed annotation 'Average grain size=32.0 µm'.

Dual-axis bar/line plot: left axis 'Grain boundary density (µm/µm²)' 0.00-0.20, right axis 'Average KAM value' 0.0-2.0; purple ATB and green HAGB bars for S0, S950, S1050, S1150 with printed values 0.044/0.035, 0.146/0.114, 0.061/0.029, 0.040/0.019; red line with circular markers shows KAM highest at S0 (between the 1.5 and 2.0 gridlines) and roughly flat at a low level for S950, S1050 and S1150.

observations.observation: Panels (a)-(d) are histograms of relative proportion (%) versus grain size (µm); x-axis spans 0-100 µm in (a)-(c) and 0-150 µm in (d).
Panel (a) has a broken y-axis (ticks 0, 2, 4, an axis-break symbol, then 55, 60, 65), showing a single bar near 1-2 µm at about 59% relative proportion.
Average grain sizes printed inside the histograms are 7.6 µm for (a), 8.7 µm for (b), 21.1 µm for (c) and 32.0 µm for (d).
Panel (e) uses two axes: left 'Grain boundary density (µm/µm²)' from 0.00 to 0.20 and right 'Average KAM value' from 0.0 to 2.0, with legend entries ATBs (purple) and HAGBs (green).
Printed bar values in (e) are, for ATBs/HAGBs respectively: S0 0.044/0.035, S950 0.146/0.114, S1050 0.061/0.029, S1150 0.040/0.019 µm/µm².

In panel (e) the red KAM curve is highest for S0 (marker between the 1.5 and 2.0 gridlines of the right axis) and drops to an almost flat low level for S950, S1050 and S1150; the individual KAM data points carry no printed numeric labels.
The caption assigns (a) to S0, (b) to S950, (c) to S1050, (d) to S1150, and (e) to 'the result of KAM value and the GB density'.
The citing text states that the maximum average grain size of 32.0 µm is achieved at the highest solution temperature of 1150 °C (Fig. 4a-d).
The citing text states that the S0 sample has an average KAM value of 1.62 and that solution treatment reduces the average KAM of S950, S1050 and S1150 to approximately 0.4.

The citing text states that S950 has the maximum densities of both ATBs and HAGBs, 0.146 and 0.114 µm/µm², and that these decrease with increasing solution temperature to minimum values of 0.040 and 0.019 µm/µm² for S1150 — values that match the numbers printed in panel (e).
The citing text links the KAM value to local residual stress, with elevated KAM corresponding to increased residual-stress accumulation and higher corrosion susceptibility.

The paper abstract describes the prepared grain-size range as 8.7-32 µm, whereas panel (a) prints an average grain size of 7.6 µm for S0; the two readings disagree and the image is taken as the direct evidence for the S0 value.
The histograms show progressive broadening of the grain-size distribution from S0 (narrow, small-grain peak) to S1150, whose bars extend well beyond 100 µm (panel d x-axis to 150 µm).

unreadable_items: panel (e): the individual KAM data points on the red line are not labelled with numeric values, so exact KAM values can only be inferred from the right-hand axis
panel (a): the exact bin widths/edge values of the grain-size histogram are not printed
